entry.title: Collider Experimental Minecraft Server Uses Parallelized Ticks
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | github.com | discussion | hacker news

Collider is an experimental Minecraft server written in Clojure that implements parallelized game ticks without using locks, regions, or thread ownership. Developed as a proof-of-concept to demonstrate performance scaling via a functional data model, the server can achieve up to 4.5 times the performance of vanilla 1.8.9 on six cores.

Unlike the regional partitioning approach used by projects like Folia, Collider's architecture does not require spatial independence between player locations. The implementation includes core mechanics such as block physics, entity AI, and light to prove the data model's ability to handle complex, interconnected game mechanics.

entry.title: Nvidia to Expand DLSS 5 Support to RTX 40-Series GPUs
entry.content:
Techmeme | theverge.com

Official support for DLSS 5 AI rendering technology will expand to GeForce RTX 40-series GPUs following an initial launch on the RTX 50-series. The company plans to roll out support for the 40-series once performance is fully optimized for the newest hardware.

Gamers will interact with the technology via a simple on-or-off toggle, while developers will have access to granular controls like Structure Intensity and semantic AI masking. These tools enable the AI to automatically distinguish between scene elements such as foliage, water, or textiles to apply customized neural lighting adjustments.

entry.title: Bit Reactor CEO Greg Foertsch Discusses Star Wars Zero Company Development
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com

Greg Foertsch, CEO and creative director of Bit Reactor, details the technical design and collaborative development processes used to create Star Wars: Zero Company. The discussion covers specific implementation details, such as in-game camera design and the studio's approach to team involvement during production.

Bit Reactor was founded by former Firaxis employees known for their work on the XCOM series. While the game has achieved significant commercial success, the studio reportedly furloughed 80 percent of its workforce leading up to the title's launch.

entry.title: Claude Fable 5 Translates 1993 Amiga Assembly for Babylonian Twins Godot Port
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | babyloniantwins.com | hacker news

The 1993 Amiga platformer Babylonian Twins has been ported to the Godot 4 engine by using Claude Fable 5 to translate 72,758 lines of 68000 assembly code. The LLM successfully reconstructed proprietary level formats and memory layouts, producing binaries that are byte-identical to the original 1993 shipped versions.

To maintain original gameplay physics, the project maintains two distinct timing standards: a 50 Hz tick rate for the assembly-based rebuild and 60 Hz for the Godot version. The implementation also bypasses standard engine physics components to replicate the specific movement and collision routines from the original source.

entry.title: Microsoft Launches Pay-As-You-Go Option for Xbox Cloud Gaming
entry.content:
Techmeme | theverge.com | source

Starting in November, users can stream eligible games through Xbox Cloud Gaming without a Game Pass subscription via a new pay-as-you-go model. Customers can purchase specific cloud playtime hours through the Xbox Store, targeting occasional gamers and those using mobile devices.

This shift occurs alongside new monthly playtime limits for Game Pass Ultimate subscribers, who will be restricted to 15 hours of cloud gaming per month. Microsoft is also testing an ad-supported free tier for Xbox Insiders as part of an effort to increase accessibility for players without a console.

entry.title: Supercell to Acquire Metacore and Merge Mansion Developer
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

An agreement has been signed for Supercell to acquire Metacore, the studio behind the mobile title Merge Mansion. The acquisition is expected to close by the end of September, integrating the game into Supercell's live games portfolio.

The deal follows a restructuring by Metacore intended to improve operational efficiency and respond to increased market competition. Supercell, a subsidiary of Tencent, continues a recent trend of expanding its mobile gaming portfolio through strategic studio acquisitions.

entry.title: Gamecity Hamburg Launches Second Round of Prototype Funding
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

Gamecity Hamburg has opened its second round of prototype funding for 2026, providing up to €80,000 in non-repayable grants to help developers create marketable video game prototypes. The funding is intended to assist studios in securing publisher deals, launching crowdfunding campaigns, or transitioning to early access.

The initiative is restricted to developers and SMEs based in or relocating to Hamburg. Applicants must have a playable prototype demonstrating core mechanics and must disclose any use of generative AI.

entry.title: CD Projekt Red to Continue Physical Releases
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com

CD Projekt Red aims to maintain physical product offerings despite the industry trend toward digital distribution. Co-CEO Michal Nowakowski announced at Gamescom 2026 that the studio will continue to provide collector-focused physical boxes, though these may increasingly utilize download codes instead of game discs to accommodate changing platform requirements.

This approach follows Sony's plan to end physical software production for PlayStation in 2028. While the studio is subject to platform-holder manufacturing decisions and the decline of disc drives, it intends to cater to collectors through high-quality physical packaging.
